daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo Subipto held a cabinet meeting on 20 July 2026 to review government programs, asserting that the administration has worked intensively and emphasizing no discrimination in anti-corruption efforts, likening corruption to cancer. The president also defended his nutritious meal program against critics and dismissed fears about negative ratings from global rating agencies. Law and Human Rights Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra confirmed that the Febrie Adriansyah corruption case was not discussed at the cabinet session.

  • The KPK conducted an arrest operation against Lombok Barat Bupati Lalu Ahmad Zaini, prompting Interior Minister to express concern that regional heads were caught despite attending anti-corruption retreats.
  • Minister Yusril said the new criminal code explains why suspect Febrie Adriansyah has not been detained, and stated he does not expect KPK to take over the case.
  • The DPR's Legislation Body completed the draft Road Traffic Bill, while Commission I backed BPKP oversight of national priority programs.
  • PDIP chairman Ganjar Pranowo called on the party to strengthen ties with the public through responsive cadres.
  • The MPR announced it is ready to approach the DPR to discuss regional bond issuance after completing its academic paper.
  • A presidential decree appointing a new attorney general for special crimes is expected to be issued this week.
  • Minister Yusril defended the Rp 5 million fee for renouncing Indonesian citizenship, saying it affects only 300 people annually and is a state revenue requirement to be complied with.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Chile strengthened cooperation in critical minerals and healthcare sectors during bilateral discussions. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that more than 1,200 Indonesian citizens have returned from online scam centres in Myanmar, and is continuing efforts to rescue two WNI still held captive there.

  • Indonesia and China conducted a joint inspection of fishery products to secure export access, with China stating it respects Indonesia's single-door export policy for strategic commodities.
  • The EU pledged support for marine conservation and coastal economies in Indonesia.
  • Pangdam XIII/Merdeka stated that the strength of TNI cavalry lies in soldier character.
  • TNI headquarters responded to reports that village NCOs have been deployed to monitor tax compliance.

Other

President Prabowo announced that state-owned bullion bank has managed 153 tons of gold in one year, and that DSI managed US$10.5 billion in forex within six weeks. He praised S&P for validating the establishment of PT DSI as appropriate. The president also reported that Indonesia has cut 250 state-owned enterprises under Danantara reform and achieved self-sufficiency in eight food commodities.

  • Energy Minister Bahlil opened the possibility of lowering Pertamax prices if global oil prices decline, and announced Indonesia targets full B50 biodiesel rollout by October.
  • Prabowo ordered the completion of 5,000 village bridges by year-end and set a target to finish all school renovations by 2029, while highlighting low teacher salaries amid economic leakage.
  • Indonesia announced it is fast-tracking permits for dairy farm investors, and President Prabowo said village cooperatives will establish supply chains down to the village level.
  • The Batam data center industry posted 22 percent annual growth, while the President hailed ITU recognition for Indonesia's education platform.
  • The Lampung port for Garibaldi carrier reached 76 percent completion, and BRIN was tasked to use technology to locate water sources.
